high.title: S.Korean investors suffer 30% losses from bonds as BOK rate hikes loom
high.summary: Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun-song indicated that South Korea's benchmark rate is expected to rise in coming months, citing stronger-than-expected growth and elevated inflation. The BOK is forecast to raise policy rates at least twice to 3.0% this year, with resilient growth giving policymakers scope to combat rising inflation. The yield on South Korea's 10-year government bond has climbed to its highest level in two and a half years as stronger growth, expansionary fiscal policy, and inflation concerns pushed investors to price in higher rates. This development has resulted in significant losses for bond investors, with some experiencing 30% declines. For fixed income investors, this signals a clear hawkish shift in BOK policy stance, making existing bonds less attractive and creating headwinds for duration strategies. The rising rate environment suggests opportunities in shorter-duration instruments while longer-dated bonds face continued pressure.

high.title: Dollar-Won Closes at 1,518.30 on Growing Optimism Over Imminent US-Iran Ceasefire Deal
high.summary: The USD/KRW exchange rate declined to 1,518.30 in overnight trading, down 10.60 won from the previous Seoul close and 1.50 won lower than the day session close of 1,519.80. The decline was driven by growing market optimism surrounding a potential US-Iran ceasefire agreement after President Trump announced that a ceasefire deal had been finalized and only required signatures. Media reports suggested both sides could sign a memorandum of understanding in Geneva on the 14th. This represents significant relief for the Korean won, which had been under pressure from geopolitical tensions. For FX traders, the development suggests potential for further won strength if the ceasefire materializes, though caution is warranted given the volatility of Middle East negotiations. The move below 1,520 is technically significant and could open the door for a test of 1,500 levels.

high.title: Presidential Office Signals FX Market Management Intent Ahead of US Investment, Says 'Exchange Rate Must Stabilize'
high.summary: The South Korean presidential office publicly emphasized the need for exchange rate stability, with a senior official stating "the exchange rate needs to stabilize" during President Lee Jae-myung's state visit to Italy. The government revealed that the US Treasury Department's exchange rate team "has a very deep understanding of our country's situation and is constantly monitoring it." This signals potential government intervention concerns as USD/KRW has been elevated. The official added that "it is important for our country, and naturally of interest to the US, that the exchange rate market moves in line with fundamentals." This represents the clearest signal yet of government vigilance toward recent won weakness and suggests possible coordinated action with US authorities. For FX markets, this indicates authorities may be preparing intervention measures if USD/KRW continues rising, creating a potential ceiling for dollar strength against the won.

medium.title: 'National Pension Rebalancing Exemption Intensified Currency Pressure' - Welfare Ministry 'Disagrees with Causality'
medium.summary: Barclays analysis suggests the National Pension Service's suspension of rebalancing in H1 2026 "functioned as an amplifier rather than a stabilizer" in FX market volatility, indirectly triggering massive foreign capital outflows. The NPS temporarily suspended rebalancing to mitigate simultaneous stock and won weakness, raising domestic equity allocation targets. This institutional policy shift appears to have had unintended consequences for currency stability.

medium.title: South Korea Growth Outlook Rises to 3.7% - Will Government Forecast Break 3%?
medium.summary: Economic growth expectations are rising rapidly due to stronger-than-anticipated semiconductor-led export boom. Attention focuses on whether the government will raise its growth forecast to the 3% range this year, which would support the BOK's hawkish stance and potentially strengthen the won through improved fundamentals.

medium.title: NDF at 1,517.20/1,517.60 Won - Down 1.05 Won
medium.summary: The dollar-won one-month NDF declined to 1,517.40 won (MID) overnight, down 1.05 won from the previous Seoul session close. The forward curve suggests continued near-term won strength expectations amid US-Iran ceasefire optimism, though some dollar firmness persists globally.

medium.title: [Market Close] Foreigners Return After 25 Trading Days on War-End Hopes - KOSPI Reclaims 8,000
medium.summary: Foreign investors turned to net buying for the first time in 25 trading sessions, purchasing 2 trillion won worth of Korean equities amid US-Iran war-end expectations. The KOSPI reclaimed 8,000 levels after a month-long 75 trillion won foreign selling spree, providing relief for the won through improved capital flows.
